### npx convex dev --start example

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/cli/reference/dev

Example of using the --start option to launch a long-running command (like a frontend dev server) alongside npx convex dev. The command inherits stdin/stdout for direct interaction.

```bash
npx convex dev --start 'vite --open'
```

### Example convex/http.js file

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/classes/server.HttpRouter

Shows how to create an HTTP router, define routes inline with httpAction, import handlers, and export the router as default. The example includes a POST route for /message and a GET route for /getMessagesByAuthor.

```javascript
import { httpRouter } from "convex/server";

import { getMessagesByAuthor } from "./getMessagesByAuthor";

import { httpAction } from "./_generated/server";



const http = httpRouter();



// HTTP actions can be defined inline...

http.route({

  path: "/message",

  method: "POST",

  handler: httpAction(async ({ runMutation }, request) => {

    const { author, body } = await request.json();



    await runMutation(api.sendMessage.default, { body, author });

    return new Response(null, {

      status: 200,

    });

  })

});



// ...or they can be imported from other files.

http.route({

  path: "/getMessagesByAuthor",

  method: "GET",

  handler: getMessagesByAuthor,

});



// Convex expects the router to be the default export of `convex/http.js`.

export default http;
```

### http.lookup() example

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/classes/server.HttpRouter

Demonstrates http.lookup() returning the appropriate HTTP action and its routed request path and method. The example shows that after routing a pathPrefix, lookup returns a tuple [getProfile, "GET", "/profile/*"] for a matching path.

```typescript
http.route({ pathPrefix: "/profile/", method: "GET", handler: getProfile});



http.lookup("/profile/abc", "GET") // returns [getProfile, "GET", "/profile/*"]
```

--------------------------------

### Query documents with db.query

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/database/reading-data

Start a document query by choosing the table with `ctx.db.query`. This example collects all tasks and is the basis for filtering, ordering, and awaiting results.

```TypeScript
import { query } from "./_generated/server";



export const listTasks = query({
  args: {},
  handler: async (ctx) => {
    const tasks = await ctx.db.query("tasks").collect();
    // do something with `tasks`
  },
});
```

### Client configuration with useAuth and Authenticated components

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/authkit/add-to-app

Example client component for a TanStack Start app using AuthKit. It uses the `useAuth` hook from `@workos/authkit-tanstack-react-start/client` for sign-out, `getAuth` for server-side user retrieval, and `convex/react`'s `Authenticated`/`Unauthenticated` components to conditionally render content. The `Content` component uses `useSuspenseQuery` with `convexQuery` to fetch data from the Convex backend.

```tsx
import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router';

import { Authenticated, Unauthenticated } from 'convex/react';

import { useAuth } from '@workos/authkit-tanstack-react-start/client';

import { getAuth } from '@workos/authkit-tanstack-react-start';

import { convexQuery } from '@convex-dev/react-query';

import { useSuspenseQuery } from '@tanstack/react-query';

import { api } from '../../convex/_generated/api';



export const Route = createFileRoute('/')({

  component: Home,

  loader: async () => {

    const { user } = await getAuth();

    return { user };

  },

});



function Home() {

  const { user } = Route.useLoaderData();

  const { signOut } = useAuth();



  return (

    <div className="p-4">

      <div className="flex justify-between items-center mb-4">

        <h1>Convex + TanStack Start + WorkOS</h1>

        {user ? (

          <button onClick={() => signOut()}>Sign out</button>

        ) : (

          <div className="flex gap-2">

            <a href="/sign-in">

              <button>Sign in</button>

            </a>

            <a href="/sign-up">

              <button>Sign up</button>

            </a>

          </div>

        )}

      </div>

      <Authenticated>

        <Content />

      </Authenticated>

      <Unauthenticated>

        <p>Please sign in to view data</p>

      </Unauthenticated>

    </div>

  );

}



function Content() {

  const { data } = useSuspenseQuery(

    convexQuery(api.myFunctions.listNumbers, { count: 10 }),

  );



  return (

    <div>

      <p>Welcome {data.viewer}!</p>

      <p>Numbers: {data.numbers?.join(', ') || 'None'}</p>

    </div>

  );
}

```

### setupConvex(url, options?)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/reactivity

Initializes the Convex client and stores it in Svelte context. Call once in a root layout. Returns a ConvexClient.

```APIDOC
## setupConvex(url, options?)

### Description
Initializes the Convex client and stores it in Svelte context. Call once in a root layout. Returns a ConvexClient.

### Function Signature
`setupConvex(url, options?)`

### Parameters
- **url** (string) - Required - The URL of the Convex deployment.
- **options** (object) - Optional - Additional options for the Convex client.

### Returns
- **ConvexClient** - The initialized Convex client.
```

### Install component with httpPrefix

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/components/using

Pass an httpPrefix when installing a component to expose its HTTP routes under that prefix. Without it, the component's routes are not exposed.

```typescript
import { defineApp } from "convex/server";

import myComponent from "./components/myComponent/convex.config.js";



const app = defineApp();

app.use(myComponent, { httpPrefix: "/my-component/" });

export default app;
```

--------------------------------

### Install Resend component and declare environment variables in convex.config.ts

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/config/convex.config.ts

Example convex.config.ts that installs the Resend component and declares environment variables. It defines RESEND_API_KEY, RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET, and an optional LOG_LEVEL, then mounts the Resend component with an HTTP prefix and passes the declared env values.

```typescript
import { defineApp } from "convex/server";

import { v } from "convex/values";

import resend from "@convex-dev/resend/convex.config.js";



const app = defineApp({

  env: {

    RESEND_API_KEY: v.string(),

    RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: v.string(),



    LOG_LEVEL: v.optional(v.union(v.literal("info"), v.literal("error"))),

  },

});



app.use(resend, {

  // Serve the Resend component’s HTTP routes

  // at `https://<deployment>.convex.site/resend/`

  httpPrefix: "/resend/",

  env: {

    RESEND_API_KEY: app.env.RESEND_API_KEY,

    RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET: app.env.RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET,

  },

});



export default app;
```

### useQueries example and result

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/modules/react

Example of using useQueries to load a query and the resulting object structure. The first block shows the hook call with a query reference and args; the second shows the returned result mapping the identifier to an array of documents.

```javascript
const results = useQueries({

  messagesInGeneral: {

    query: "listMessages",

    args: { channel: "#general" }

  }

});
```

```javascript
{

  messagesInGeneral: [{

    channel: "#general",

    body: "hello"

    _id: ...,

    _creationTime: ...

  }]

}
```

### Infer type from validator

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/modules/values

Extracts the TypeScript type from a validator using the Infer type. The example creates an object schema with v.object and v.string, then uses Infer to get the corresponding type.

```typescript
const objectSchema = v.object({

  property: v.string(),

});

type MyObject = Infer<typeof objectSchema>; // { property: string }
```

### Structuring SwiftUI app with ViewModel: ObservableObject

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/swift

Adapts the colors:get example into a ViewModel: ObservableObject class. The View observes the ViewModel as a @StateObject and rebuilds when it changes, decoupling the View from direct data fetching.

```swift
import SwiftUI
class ViewModel: ObservableObject {
  @Published var colors: [String] = []
  init() {
    convex.subscribe(to: "colors:get")
      .replaceError(with: [])
      .receive(on: DispatchQueue.main)
      .assign(to: &$colors)
  }
}
struct ContentView: View {
  @StateObject var viewModel = ViewModel()
  var body: some View {
    List {
      ForEach(viewModel.colors, id: \.self) { color in
        Text(color)
      }
    }
  }
}
```

--------------------------------

### Install OpenAI SDK and call models via AI Gateway action

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/setup

Install the openai package and configure the OpenAI client with the AI Gateway base URL and dynamic service token in a Convex action.

```bash
npm install openai
```

```typescript
import { action } from "./_generated/server";

import { v } from "convex/values";

import OpenAI from "openai";

import { getServiceToken } from "convex/server";



export const chat = action({

  args: { prompt: v.string() },

  handler: async (ctx, { prompt }) => {

    const openai = new OpenAI({

      baseURL: "https://ai-gateway.convex.dev/v1",

      apiKey: () => getServiceToken("ai-gateway"),

    });

    const completion = await openai.chat.completions.create({

      model: "openai/gpt-4o-mini",

      messages: [{ role: "user", content: prompt }],

    });

    return completion.choices[0].message.content;

  },

});
```

--------------------------------

### Start asynchronous video generation with experimental_startVideo

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/images-and-videos

Starts an asynchronous video generation job with Convex AI Gateway. Requires creating a job record beforehand to pass its requestId and saving the returned operation handle, inferenceId, and webhookSecret.

```typescript
import { experimental_startVideo as startVideo } from "ai";

import { convexGateway } from "@convex-dev/ai-sdk-provider";



async function startJob(requestId: string) {

  const modelId = "google/veo-3.1";

  const started = await startVideo({

    model: convexGateway.videoModel(modelId),

    prompt: "A camera pan across a mountain lake",

    duration: 8,

    webhookUrl: `${process.env.CONVEX_SITE_URL}/video-complete?requestId=${requestId}`,

    maxRetries: 0,

  });



  return {

    modelId,

    operation: started.operation,

    inferenceId: started.providerMetadata?.convexGateway?.inferenceId,

    webhookSecret: started.providerMetadata?.convexGateway?.webhookSecret,

  };

}
```

### One-off query via useConvex() in React

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/react

Use the useConvex() hook to get the ConvexReactClient and call its async query method outside of a subscription, for example to validate input in a callback. The query method is used without making changes to the database; it returns the data fetched.

```tsx
import { useConvex } from "convex/react";
import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";
export function App() {
  const convex = useConvex();
  return (
    <button
      onClick={async () => {
        console.log(await convex.query(api.functions.myQuery));
      }}
    >
      Check
    </button>
  );
}

```

### Create main.py to query and subscribe to tasks

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/python

Creates a ConvexClient, loads the CONVEX_URL from .env.local, queries the "tasks:get" API, and subscribes to it, printing each update. The subscription loop runs indefinitely until interrupted.

```python
import os
from convex import ConvexClient
from dotenv import load_dotenv

load_dotenv(".env.local")
CONVEX_URL = os.getenv("CONVEX_URL")
# or you can hardcode your deployment URL instead
# CONVEX_URL = "https://happy-otter-123.convex.cloud"

client = ConvexClient(CONVEX_URL)
print(client.query("tasks:get"))
for tasks in client.subscribe("tasks:get"):
    print(tasks)
    # this loop lasts forever, ctrl-c to exit it
```

--------------------------------

### useQuery example with loading state and skip

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/modules/react

Example usage of useQuery from the Convex React client. It loads tasks with a filter and handles the undefined loading state. It also shows how to conditionally disable the query by passing 'skip' as an argument.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "convex/react";

import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";



function TaskList() {

  // Reactively loads tasks, re-renders when data changes:

  const tasks = useQuery(api.tasks.list, { completed: false });



  // Returns `undefined` while loading:

  if (tasks === undefined) return <div>Loading...</div>;



  return tasks.map((task) => <div key={task._id}>{task.text}</div>);

}



// Pass "skip" to conditionally disable the query:

function MaybeProfile({ userId }: { userId?: Id<"users"> }) {

  const profile = useQuery(

    api.users.get,

    userId ? { userId } : "skip",

  );

  // ...

}
```

### setupAuth

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/authentication

The setupAuth function integrates authentication with Convex by accepting a reactive getter that provides the auth provider's state and automatically manages the Convex client's authentication lifecycle.

```APIDOC
## setupAuth

### Description
Sets up authentication for the Convex Svelte client by accepting a reactive getter that returns the auth provider's state. It automatically manages `client.setAuth()` and `client.clearAuth()` based on changes in the provider state.

### Method
setupAuth

### Parameters
- **getter** (function) - Required - A reactive getter that returns an object with the following properties:
  - `isLoading` (boolean) - Indicates if authentication is in progress.
  - `isAuthenticated` (boolean) - Indicates if the user is authenticated.
  - `fetchAccessToken` (async function) - A function that returns an access token. It receives an object with `forceRefreshToken` property.

### Example
```ts
setupAuth(() => ({
  isLoading: false,
  isAuthenticated: !!session,
  fetchAccessToken: async ({ forceRefreshToken }) => {
    if (!session) return null;
    return await getTokenFromYourAuthProvider({ forceRefreshToken });
  },
}));
```
```

### Create test.setup.ts with import.meta.glob

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/testing/convex-test

```typescript
/// <reference types="vite/client" />

export const modules = import.meta.glob(

  "./**/!(*.*.*)*.*s"

);
```

### experimental_startVideo(options)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/images-and-videos

Initiates an asynchronous video generation request through the Convex AI Gateway and returns an operation identifier and job metadata.

```APIDOC
### Function
`experimental_startVideo(options: StartVideoOptions): Promise<StartVideoResult>`

### Description
Starts an asynchronous video generation task. Used when actions should return before video generation completes.

### Parameters
- **model** (`VideoModel`) - Required. The configured video model instance, e.g. `convexGateway.videoModel(modelId)`.
- **prompt** (`string`) - Required. Text prompt describing the video to generate.
- **duration** (`number`) - Optional. Duration of the generated video in seconds.
- **webhookUrl** (`string`) - Optional. HTTPS callback URL (`<deployment>.convex.site`) to receive completion notifications.
- **maxRetries** (`number`) - Optional. Number of submission retries (e.g., `0` to prevent automatic duplicate paid jobs).

### Return Value
Returns a promise resolving to an object containing:
- **operation** (`string`) - The operation handle to check status or download the result.
- **providerMetadata.convexGateway.inferenceId** (`string`) - Unique inference ID associated with the job.
- **providerMetadata.convexGateway.webhookSecret** (`string`) - Secret key used to verify incoming webhook callbacks.
```

--------------------------------

### useQuery

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/reactivity

Documentation for the useQuery hook from convex-svelte, including its signature, options, return value, and usage examples.

```APIDOC
## useQuery

### Description
Subscribes to a Convex query with automatic real-time updates. When the data changes on the server, the component re-renders automatically.

### Method
useQuery

### Signature
useQuery(query, argsFunction, options?)

### Parameters
- **query** (Function) - Required - The Convex query function, typically from the generated `api` object.
- **argsFunction** (Function) - Required - A function that returns the arguments object for the query, or `'skip'` to skip the query.
- **options** (Object) - Optional - Configuration options.
  - **initialData** (any) - Optional - Pre-loaded data for SSR/hydration, avoids the loading state.
  - **keepPreviousData** (boolean) - Optional - When `true`, keeps displaying the previous result while new data loads after args change.

### Return Value
The returned object is reactive and has the following shape:
- **data** (T | undefined) - The query result, or `undefined` while loading.
- **error** (Error | undefined) - The error, if the query failed.
- **isLoading** (boolean) - `true` until the first result or error is received.
- **isStale** (boolean) - `true` when displaying cached data from previous arguments.

### Skipping Queries
You can conditionally skip a query by returning `'skip'` from the arguments function. When a query is skipped, `isLoading` will be `false`, `error` will be `null`, and `data` will be `undefined`.

### Example
```svelte
<script lang="ts">
  import { useQuery } from "convex-svelte";
  import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api.js";

  const messages = useQuery(api.messages.list, () => ({ searchWords }), {
    keepPreviousData: true,
  });
</script>

{#if messages.isLoading}
  Loading...
{:else if messages.error != null}
  failed to load: {messages.error.toString()}
{:else}
  <ul>
    {#each messages.data as message}
      <li>
        <span>{message.author}</span>
        <span>{message.body}</span>
      </li>
    {/each}
  </ul>
{/if}
```
```

--------------------------------

### Run tests

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/testing/convex-test

```bash
npm run test
```

### Generate Go client with openapi-generator-cli

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/open-api

Installs openapi-generator-cli and creates a type-safe Go client package inside the convex_client directory using convex-spec.yaml.

```shell
npm i openapi-generator-cli

npx openapi-generator-cli generate -i convex-spec.yaml -g go -o convex_client
```

### GET /teams/:team_id/list_deployment_classes

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/management-api/list-deployment-classes

This endpoint lists the available deployment classes for a team. It is a GET request to the /teams/:team_id/list_deployment_classes endpoint.

```APIDOC
## GET /teams/:team_id/list_deployment_classes

### Description
Lists the available deployment classes for a team.

### Method
GET

### Endpoint
/teams/:team_id/list_deployment_classes

### Parameters
#### Path Parameters
- **team_id** (string) - Required - The unique identifier of the team.

### Response
#### Success Response (200)
Returns a list of deployment classes available for the specified team.

```

### Install TypeScript 7

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/cli/troubleshooting/typecheck-performance

Install TypeScript 7 as the project's TypeScript version to use its faster native compiler. Convex will automatically use it. Note that TypeScript 7.0 does not include a JavaScript API; follow side-by-side installation instructions if other tools need it.

```bash
npm install --save-dev typescript@^7
```

### Create preview deployment and seed data with --preview-create and --preview-run

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/production/multiple-deployments

Creates a preview deployment and runs a Convex function to seed initial data. Replace <functionName> with the name of a Convex function that runs only if a preview deployment is created. --preview-run is ignored if npx convex deploy doesn't create a preview deployment. If the function call fails, the deploy command fails but the preview deployment is already provisioned.

```bash
npx convex deploy --preview-create="my-preview-deployment-name" --preview-run=<functionName>
```

--------------------------------

### Query Convex backend from src/main.rs

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/rust

Connect to Convex using `ConvexClient` with the deployment URL from the environment and query the `tasks:get` API.

```rust
use std::{

    collections::BTreeMap,

    env,

};



use convex::ConvexClient;



#[tokio::main]

async fn main() {

    dotenvy::from_filename(".env.local").ok();

    dotenvy::dotenv().ok();



    let deployment_url = env::var("CONVEX_URL").unwrap();



    let mut client = ConvexClient::new(&deployment_url).await.unwrap();

    let result = client.query("tasks:get", BTreeMap::new()).await.unwrap();

    println!("{result:#?}");

}
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize ConvexClient with setupConvex in root layout

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/svelte/overview

Calls `setupConvex` in the root layout to initialize the client and make it accessible across child components via Svelte context.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">

  import { setupConvex } from "convex-svelte";

  import { PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL } from "$env/static/public";



  const client = setupConvex(PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL);

</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Set up Convex in src/routes/+layout.svelte

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/svelte

Initializes setupConvex with PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL at the root layout to make Convex available across the entire app.

```svelte
<script lang="ts">

	import { PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL } from '$env/static/public';

	import { setupConvex } from 'convex-svelte';



	const { children } = $props();

	setupConvex(PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL);

</script>



{@render children()}
```

### Scheduler Interface

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/interfaces/server.Scheduler

Documentation for the Scheduler interface, including the runAfter method, execution guarantees, and an example usage.

```APIDOC
## Scheduler Interface

### Description
An interface to schedule Convex functions to run in the future. Available as `ctx.scheduler` in mutations and actions.

### Methods

#### runAfter(delayMs, functionReference, args)

Schedules a function to run after a specified delay.

- **delayMs** (number) - The delay in milliseconds before the function runs.
- **functionReference** (FunctionReference) - The reference to the function to run. Use `internal` functions to prevent direct client calls.
- **args** (object) - The arguments to pass to the scheduled function.

**Execution Guarantees:**
- Scheduled mutations execute exactly once and are automatically retried on transient errors.
- Scheduled actions execute at most once and are not retried.

**Example:**
```ts
import { mutation } from "./_generated/server";
import { internal } from "./_generated/api";
import { v } from "convex/values";

export const createOrder = mutation({
  args: { items: v.array(v.string()) },
  returns: v.null(),
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const orderId = await ctx.db.insert("orders", { items: args.items });

    // Run immediately after this mutation commits:
    await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(0, internal.emails.sendConfirmation, {
      orderId,
    });

    // Run cleanup in 7 days:
    await ctx.scheduler.runAfter(
      7 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000,
      internal.orders.archiveOrder,
      { orderId },
    );

    return null;
  },
});
```

**See Also:**
- [Scheduled Functions Documentation](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions)
```

### ConvexError data payload examples

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/functions/error-handling/application-errors

Three examples showing how to pass strings or objects to the ConvexError constructor, with the resulting error.data values.

```typescript
// error.data === "My fancy error message"

throw new ConvexError("My fancy error message");



// error.data === {message: "My fancy error message", code: 123, severity: "high"}

throw new ConvexError({

  message: "My fancy error message",

  code: 123,

  severity: "high",

});



// error.data === {code: 123, severity: "high"}

throw new ConvexError({

  code: 123,

  severity: "high",

});
```

### Connect the app to your backend (src/main.tsx)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/react

In src/main.tsx, create a ConvexReactClient and pass it to a ConvexProvider wrapping your app.

```tsx
import React from "react";import ReactDOM from "react-dom/client";import App from "./App";import "./index.css";import { ConvexProvider, ConvexReactClient } from "convex/react";const convex = new ConvexReactClient(import.meta.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL as string);ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")!).render(  <React.StrictMode>    <ConvexProvider client={convex}>      <App />    </ConvexProvider>  </React.StrictMode>,);
```

### Get URL for a stored file

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/interfaces/server.StorageReader

Gets the URL for a file in storage by its Id<"_storage">. Returns null if the file no longer exists.

```typescript
const url = await ctx.storage.getUrl(storageId);
```

--------------------------------

### Incorrect conditional useQuery call

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/react

Shows an error example where useQuery is called conditionally, which violates React Hooks rules. This is presented as a cautionary example.

```tsx
import { useQuery } from "convex/react";
import { api } from "../convex/_generated/api";
export function App() {
  // the URL `param` might be null
  const param = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("param");
  // ERROR! React Hook "useQuery" is called conditionally. React Hooks must
  // be called in the exact same order in every component render.
  const data = param !== null ? useQuery(api.functions.read, { param }) : null;
  //...
}
```

### getUrl(storageId)

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/interfaces/server.StorageReader

Get the URL for a file in storage by its `Id<"_storage">`. The GET response includes a standard HTTP Digest header with a sha256 checksum.

```APIDOC
## getUrl(storageId)

### Description
Get the URL for a file in storage by its `Id<"_storage">`. The GET response includes a standard HTTP Digest header with a sha256 checksum.

### Method
`getUrl`

### Parameters
- `storageId` (`GenericId<"_storage">`) - Required - The `Id<"_storage">` of the file to fetch from Convex storage.

### Returns
`Promise<null | string>` - A URL which fetches the file via an HTTP GET, or `null` if the file no longer exists.

### Example
```
const url = await ctx.storage.getUrl(storageId);
```

### Deprecated Overload
Passing a string is deprecated, use `storage.getUrl(Id<"_storage">)` instead.

#### Parameters
- `storageId` (`T extends { __tableName: any } ? never : T`) - Required - The `StorageId` of the file to fetch from Convex storage.

#### Returns
`Promise<null | string>` - A url which fetches the file via an HTTP GET, or `null` if it no longer exists.
```

--------------------------------

### Connect to Convex via script tag in index.html

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/quickstart/script-tag

Loads the Convex browser bundle via unpkg script tag, initializes ConvexClient with CONVEX_URL, and subscribes to real-time updates from tasks:get.

```html
<!doctype html>

<script src="https://unpkg.com/convex@1.3.1/dist/browser.bundle.js"></script>

<script>

  const CONVEX_URL = "CONVEX_URL_GOES_HERE";

  const client = new convex.ConvexClient(CONVEX_URL);

  client.onUpdate("tasks:get", {}, (tasks) =>

    console.log(tasks.map((task) => task.text)),

  );

</script>
```

--------------------------------

### Set up environment variables in .env.local

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/auth/authkit/add-to-app

Example .env.local file with WorkOS and Convex environment variables. WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD must be at least 32 characters and can be generated with `openssl rand -base64 24`. NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI must match the WorkOS Dashboard configuration.

```dotenv
# WorkOS AuthKit Configuration

WORKOS_CLIENT_ID=client_your_client_id_here

WORKOS_API_KEY=sk_test_your_api_key_here

WORKOS_COOKIE_PASSWORD=your_secure_password_here_must_be_at_least_32_characters_long

NEXT_PUBLIC_WORKOS_REDIRECT_URI=http://localhost:3000/callback



# Convex Configuration (you don't have to fill these out, they're generated by Convex)

# Deployment used by `npx convex dev`

CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=your_convex_deploy_key_here

NEXT_PUBLIC_CONVEX_URL=https://your-convex-url.convex.cloud
```

--------------------------------

### get

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/interfaces/server.GenericDatabaseWriter

The get method is used to fetch a single document from the database. It has two overloads: one that takes a table name and an id, and another that takes only an id for backwards compatibility.

```APIDOC
## get(table, id)

### Description
Fetches a single document from the database by table name and GenericId.

### Method
`get`

### Parameters
- `table` (TableName) - Required - The name of the table to fetch the document from.
- `id` (GenericId<NonUnion<TableName>>) - Required - The GenericId of the document to fetch from the database.

### Returns
`Promise<null | DocumentByName<DataModel, TableName>>` - The GenericDocument of the document at the given GenericId, or `null` if it no longer exists.

### Example
```
const user = await ctx.db.get("users", userId);
```
```

```APIDOC
## get(id)

### Description
Fetches a single document from the database by its GenericId. Supported for backwards compatibility. Prefer `db.get(tableName, id)` in new code, or `db.system.get(tableName, id)` for system tables.

### Method
`get`

### Parameters
- `id` (GenericId<TableName>) - Required - The GenericId of the document to fetch from the database.

### Returns
`Promise<null | DocumentByName<DataModel, TableName>>` - The GenericDocument of the document at the given GenericId, or `null` if it no longer exists.
```

### usePaginatedQuery example

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/api/modules/react

Example usage of usePaginatedQuery to load paginated data. It passes a query reference, arguments, and options with initialNumItems. The hook returns results, status, isLoading, and loadMore.

```typescript
const { results, status, isLoading, loadMore } = usePaginatedQuery(

  api.messages.list,

  { channel: "#general" },

  { initialNumItems: 5 }

);
```

### Create a ConvexClient instance

Source: https://docs.convex.dev/client/android/overview

Create a ConvexClient instance by providing your backend deployment URL. Use one instance for the lifetime of your application process.

```kotlin
package com.example.convexapp



import dev.convex.android.ConvexClient



val convex = ConvexClient("https://<your domain here>.convex.cloud")
```
